metadata.name: MillLedger Design System
metadata.productType: responsive operations, inventory, purchasing, production and sales PWA
metadata.measurementPolicy: Always display the unit beside a quantity; never leave a number dimensionally ambiguous.
metadata.purpose: A concrete, implementation-oriented visual and interaction system for the CDI NITT internship selection assignment. The system is designed to make operational work legible, verifiable and calm.

designIntent.oneSentence: A quiet, dependable workshop ledger: warm paper surfaces, deep evergreen actions, crisp data typography and explicit operational state.
designIntent.visualMetaphor: A well-kept production ledger translated into a modern, responsive interface.
informationPriority: The current record and its state

visualHierarchy.pageTitle: One clear page title, with a short purpose line where it adds context.
visualHierarchy.primaryAction: One visually dominant action per work area; secondary actions use quieter styles.
visualHierarchy.operationalData: Tables and ledger rows are first-class content, not content hidden inside decorative cards.
visualHierarchy.status: A readable status label plus icon or shape; color is a supporting signal only.
visualHierarchy.supportingVisuals: Use small, labelled process diagrams, timelines, measured charts and purposeful empty-state illustrations when they reduce explanation time.

avoid: AI sparkles, robot motifs, glows or generative-looking decoration
Large hero typography inside operational portals
A grid of identical KPI cards on every page
Cards nested inside cards without a clear grouping purpose
Decorative glass, blur, parallax, floating blobs or excessive shadows
Bouncy motion, staggered page-load choreography or count-up numbers
Color-only statuses, unlabeled icon controls and placeholder-only form labels
Fake charts, fake percentages, ambiguous units or unexplained abbreviations
Using modals for routine information or toast notifications for field errors

principles.rule: Start each screen from the user's task, the record being changed and the worst plausible mistake.
principles.implementation: Define the primary task, consequence, data needed, permission and recovery path before styling the screen.

principles.rule: Prefer clear tables, record details, timelines and task queues over a wall of generic metric cards.
principles.implementation: Use cards only to group genuinely related content or isolate a consequential summary.

principles.rule: Every consequential action must show whether it is draft, saving, posted, failed, queued or awaiting review.
principles.implementation: Show feedback near the action and preserve the resulting state in the record itself.

principles.rule: A color has a stable semantic meaning across all portals.
principles.implementation: Pine means primary action/selected navigation; green means successful state; amber means attention; red means destructive or blocking; blue means informational.

principles.rule: Prevent invalid quantities, duplicate actions, accidental posting and irreversible mistakes before they happen.
principles.implementation: Use input constraints, inline validation, review summaries, clear permissions and server-confirmed commit states.

principles.rule: Motion must explain a state change, preserve spatial context or confirm an action.
principles.implementation: Prefer short opacity and small-position transitions. Remove motion when it adds no information.

principles.rule: Keyboard, touch, zoom, contrast and reduced-motion support are baseline requirements.
principles.implementation: Design to WCAG 2.2 AA; voluntarily use 44px touch targets and reduced-motion behavior as stronger product defaults.

principles.rule: Never show a committed financial or inventory result before the server confirms it.
principles.implementation: Optimistic updates are restricted to reversible, low-risk UI preferences; transactions wait for the authoritative response.

researchBasis.sourceNature: Heuristics are broad rules of thumb, not a substitute for user testing or task-specific requirements.

application: use color consistently and do not rely on color alone
provide a clear press state and generous target areas
researchBasis.sourceNature: Apple's HIG is platform guidance; MillLedger borrows the underlying interaction principles rather than copying iOS visual styling.

application: loading patterns selected by wait type and duration
data-table numeric alignment, sticky context and density
consistent easing and short feedback motion
optimistic updates restricted to reversible, low-stakes actions
researchBasis.sourceNature: A useful practitioner resource, not a normative accessibility or usability standard. Individual recommendations are treated as hypotheses and adapted to MillLedger's operational risk.

application: 4.5:1 normal text contrast and 3:1 large text contrast
3:1 non-text contrast for meaningful controls and graphics
reflow at 320 CSS px without loss of information or functionality
minimum pointer target size of 24 by 24 CSS px, subject to stated exceptions
review/confirmation or reversibility for financial and data-changing actions
researchBasis.sourceNature: Normative accessibility success criteria. The product must still be tested in rendered components and workflows; token values alone do not prove conformance.

usageRules: Never use status colors as brand decoration.
Never rely on color alone; pair status color with a text label and an icon or shape.
Never use muted text for essential instructions unless its contrast is checked on the actual adjacent surface.
Use control-border tokens for input and interactive boundaries; subtle separators are not a substitute for a visible control boundary.
Do not place text on low-contrast backgrounds merely because the palette swatch looks attractive.
Use the same semantic state color in every portal and table.

family.primary: Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif
family.delivery: If Inter is selected, self-host a variable WOFF2 file in the application. Do not depend on a third-party font CDN for core UI rendering. System UI remains the fallback.

numeric.alignment: Right-align numeric table columns; align units consistently and keep unit labels visible.

contentRules: Use sentence case for headings, buttons and statuses.
Do not use all-caps for long labels or navigation.
Use bold for hierarchy, not for decoration.
Keep body text at 14px or larger for routine operational content.
Use 16px or larger form-control text on mobile to avoid browser zoom behavior and improve legibility.
Do not use text inside images when live text can provide the same information.

rules: Use 6px for inputs and buttons, 8px for compact status pills and menus, 10-12px for panels where the grouping needs a container.
Avoid rounding every nested element.
Avoid oversized pill buttons except for compact chips or segmented controls.

borders.style: Use one-pixel separators for grouping; use higher-contrast control borders for inputs and interactive boundaries.
borders.focusRing: 3px solid #176B54 with 2px offset in light mode; use theme semantic token in dark mode.

usage.content-panels: Prefer borders and surface tone; no default card shadow.
usage.sticky-table-header: separator line; shadow only where scrolling requires depth cue

compact.useWhen: Dense operational datasets on desktop; preserve at least 44px interactive hit areas for controls inside rows.

comfortable.useWhen: Default density and mixed pointer/touch environments.

motion.principle: Motion clarifies cause, location or state. It must not delay the user's next action.
rules: Do not animate every page load, dashboard metric or table row.
Do not use bounce, elastic overshoot, spring effects or scroll-driven animation in routine workflows.
Do not animate numeric values to create excitement; update values directly and provide textual context.
Do not animate layout geometry in ways that cause content to jump or shift.
Do not use motion as the only indication that a save, error or selection occurred.
Do not use a 50ms stagger for ordinary table rows; render operational data immediately.
Use linear easing only for continuous progress/spinner rotation, not for entrance or state transitions.
Motion should start on the user's action, never after an arbitrary delay.

reducedMotion.policy: Remove nonessential transforms, sliding and animated progression. Use immediate state replacement or a brief opacity change. Keep progress/status information available without animation.
reducedMotion.css: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { *, *::before, *::after { scroll-behavior: auto !important; animation-duration: 0.01ms !important; animation-iteration-count: 1 !important; transition-duration: 0.01ms !important; } }

button.minWidth: 44px for icon-only controls; label-first for primary actions

variants.primary: One key action per view, e.g. Add item, Create purchase, Record payment.
variants.secondary: Useful supporting action, e.g. Export, Save draft.
variants.tertiary: Low-emphasis action such as Cancel or View details.
variants.destructive: Delete, void or irreversible action; use only when action is genuinely destructive.

button.loadingBehavior: Keep the button width stable, prevent duplicate submission, show a small spinner and action-specific text such as 'Saving…' or 'Posting…'.
button.labelRule: Use a verb plus object. Avoid vague labels such as Submit, Proceed or OK when the outcome can be named.

formField.labelPosition: Visible label above the control; never rely on placeholder text as the only label.
formField.focus: 3px focus ring with 2px offset; keep visible for keyboard navigation.
formField.helperText: Place persistent instructions immediately below the field.

validation.initial: Do not show a red error before the user has interacted with the field or attempted submission.
validation.timing: Validate on blur and on submit; after an error appears, revalidate as the user corrects that field.
validation.error: Place a short, actionable message next to the field and link it programmatically with aria-describedby.
validation.success: Only show a positive field state when the check adds meaningful certainty; avoid a green check on every ordinary text input.

formField.required: Use explicit required indication and explain the meaning once per form.

quantityInput.behavior: Numeric input with visible unit, decimal precision and allowed range.
quantityInput.layout: Keep the unit outside the editable value where possible, e.g. [ 125.50 ] [ kg ].
validation: Reject negative quantity where the domain does not allow it.
Show available stock or production limit in nearby helper text when relevant.
Do not silently round entered values.
Display the allowed precision and unit before submission.

rules: Use decimal-safe arithmetic in the data layer; formatting must not alter stored precision.
Keep currency visible in labels or values.
Do not hide tax, discount or total calculation assumptions.
Show subtotal, adjustments, tax and grand total in a review summary before posting.

statusBadge.content: Icon or shape plus explicit text label.
never: color-only dot as the only status indication
ambiguous labels such as Active when a domain-specific state is available

dataTable.implementation: Use semantic table markup for tabular data. Do not simulate a table with generic divs.
dataTable.header: Sticky when vertical scrolling requires it; preserve column labels.
dataTable.numericColumns: Right-aligned with tabular figures; include the unit in the header or value.
dataTable.sorting: Expose current sort field and direction; provide a deterministic return to default order.
dataTable.selection: Use a visible selected-row treatment and a usable checkbox target. Expose indeterminate select-all state.
dataTable.density: Use compact, comfortable and touch density tokens consistently.
dataTable.filters: Show active filters as removable chips and provide a clear-all action.
dataTable.empty: Explain why the table is empty and the next useful action; distinguish no records from no search matches.
dataTable.loading: Use skeleton rows only when the expected row structure is known; preserve header and layout.
dataTable.error: Keep the table context, explain the failure and offer Retry without wiping active filters.
dataTable.mobile: Avoid page-wide horizontal overflow. Reflow nonessential columns into record details; when a genuine multi-column table must scroll, keep the scroll region explicit and the identifying column anchored.

useFor: Reviewing and confirming a high-impact action
A blocking decision that cannot safely proceed in the current context
avoidFor: Every low-risk delete or reversible action
dialog.behavior: Move focus into the dialog, contain focus while open, support Escape when safe, and return focus to the invoking control on close.
dialog.transactionReview: Show the record, amount/quantity, affected stock or balances, and consequence before final commit.

toast.position: Bottom-right desktop; top edge on mobile, away from critical controls.
rules: Never use a toast as the only place where a field error appears.
Never move keyboard focus to a routine toast.
Pause auto-dismiss while hovered or keyboard-focused.
Provide Undo only when a real, safe undo operation exists.
Do not use a toast to claim a server transaction succeeded before commit.

useFor: Stock discrepancy or unresolved operational exception
Important sync state that affects several records
banner.behavior: Persistent until resolved or explicitly dismissed where dismissal is safe; include an action when the user can resolve it.

emptyState.visual: Small, purposeful line illustration or process pictogram accompanied by clear text.

example.title: No stock items yet
example.description: Add the materials your team buys, stores or uses in production.

emptyState.avoid: Large generic illustration, decorative gradients or an empty panel with only a vague sentence.

processTimeline.visual: Connected steps with status, timestamp, actor and record link.
processTimeline.rule: Show completed, current, blocked and future steps with both icon/shape and text.

chart.default: Prefer horizontal bar comparisons or a clearly labelled line chart when trend is meaningful.
requirements: Every chart has a title, period, units and a short plain-language summary.
Provide an accessible data table or equivalent text summary.
Use marker/line-style differences as well as color where series must be distinguished.
Do not truncate axes in a way that exaggerates change without making the scale explicit.
Do not use a chart when a small table is faster to compare.

navigation.desktop: Persistent left navigation with clear current location; keep high-frequency work areas near the top.
navigation.mobile: Compact top bar plus drawer; use bottom navigation only for a small, stable set of the most-used destinations.
navigation.rule: Keep route changes predictable, preserve filters and table context when returning from a record.

pageHeader.rule: The page title must name the work area, not a marketing phrase.

forms.grouping: Group fields by the user's task and real-world document structure, not by database tables.
forms.sequence: Identity and date → line items/details → calculations → notes/attachments → review.
forms.saveDraft: Use explicit Save draft when a record can remain incomplete.
forms.unsavedChanges: Warn before leaving only when unsaved data would actually be lost; keep entered values on validation failure.
forms.reviewStep: For high-impact records, show a review step with a clear edit path before final posting.

inventory.recordDetail: Show current quantity, unit, reorder threshold, storage location, latest movement and full movement history.
inventory.stockAdjustment: Require adjustment reason; show quantity before, change and quantity after before commit.
inventory.lowStock: Show numeric threshold and shortfall, not only a warning badge.
inventory.negativeStock: Do not communicate negative stock as an ordinary success state; show a blocking validation or explicit policy exception path.

purchaseLifecycle: Closed or reversed by an auditable correction
purchasing.receiving: Show ordered, received, remaining and accepted/rejected quantities per line.
purchasing.feedback: Explain how posting the receipt changes available stock.

production.batchDetail: Use a process timeline: planned inputs → issued materials → production output → quality/acceptance → finished-goods stock.
production.quantityReview: Show planned, actual, rejected/scrap and accepted output with units before completion.
production.variance: Show the variance as a value and explain whether it is within configured tolerance.

salesAndPayments.financialReview: Display party, reference, line items, totals, payment status and remaining balance before final action.
salesAndPayments.posting: Wait for server confirmation. Do not optimistically display a posted invoice, completed payment or settled balance.
salesAndPayments.correction: Use an auditable reversal/correction flow with a reason rather than silently editing a posted record.

searchAndFilters.search: Search by the identifiers users actually know: item name/code, party, invoice/reference or batch number.
searchAndFilters.filters: Keep filter state visible and removable; preserve it in the URL when practical.
searchAndFilters.results: Show result count and the active scope; distinguish no matches from no records.

bulkActions.behavior: Only reveal actions valid for the selected records and the user's permissions.
bulkActions.review: Show selected count and summarize affected records before applying high-impact changes.
bulkActions.keyboard: Support keyboard selection and bulk action invocation.

dragAndDrop.policy: Never make dragging the only way to perform an action.
dragAndDrop.alternative: Provide Move up/down, reorder menu, numeric position field or explicit destination control.

feedbackSystem.principle: Feedback is a truthful statement about the system state, not decoration.

loading.pattern: No loading indicator; avoid a flash.

loading.condition: Initial content load above 300ms and the content silhouette is known
loading.pattern: Skeleton for the affected table/list region; retain headings and surrounding layout.

loading.condition: Short action with unknown duration, typically below 3 seconds
loading.pattern: Inline spinner in the initiating control plus action text such as Saving…; block duplicate submit.
Determinate progress bar with percentage and meaningful stage/remaining-time context.
Indeterminate progress plus a truthful stage label; never invent a percentage.

loading.condition: Refresh while valid previous data exists
loading.pattern: Keep the previous result visible, mark it as refreshing and prevent stale data from appearing freshly committed.

examples: Purchase PUR-1042 posted. Stock balances have been updated.
requirements: Only report success after authoritative server confirmation.
Update the record's persistent status and activity history.
Use a concise toast as secondary feedback, not as the only record of success.

error.messagePattern: What failed + what remains unchanged + the next safe action.
examples: Payment was not recorded. No balance was changed. Check the payment details and try again.
This receipt exceeds the remaining purchase quantity by 12 kg. Reduce the received quantity or review the purchase.
requirements: Use plain language; avoid raw stack traces and unexplained codes.
Keep the user's input and context.
Place field errors beside the fields; provide a summary for multi-field submit failures.
Give a recovery action when one is known.
Announce important asynchronous status changes to assistive technology.

offlineAndSync.offline: Persistent banner: Offline. You can continue with actions supported on this device.
offlineAndSync.queued: Explicit label: Saved on this device · Waiting to sync.
offlineAndSync.conflict: Needs review · This change conflicts with newer server data.
offlineAndSync.failed: Sync failed · Your local draft is still available. Retry or review the conflict.
rules: Do not describe a local queue entry as server-saved.
Do not reserve or decrement server stock optimistically while offline.
Keep a visible queue count and per-record sync state.
Never silently discard a queued action or overwrite server data after a conflict.

destructiveAndHighImpact.lowRiskReversible: Perform the action and offer a meaningful Undo where an actual reversal is supported.
destructiveAndHighImpact.irreversibleOrHighImpact: Require a review/confirmation step that states the consequence and identifies the affected record.
destructiveAndHighImpact.postedRecords: Use append-only correction or reversal with reason and actor; do not silently mutate posted financial or stock records.
destructiveAndHighImpact.duplicateSubmission: Disable repeat submit while pending and use server-side idempotency; the UI must still show the final authoritative result.

notificationSurface.inline: Field-specific validation or a status tied to a specific record.
notificationSurface.banner: Persistent system-level condition or operational exception.
notificationSurface.dialog: A decision or confirmation that must be resolved before continuing.
notificationSurface.badge: A quiet count or flag attached to a navigation item; never the only explanation.

dataVisualization.purpose: Help an operator spot a condition or compare values, not decorate a dashboard.
preferredForms: horizontal bars for category or threshold comparisons
stacked bars only where components of a whole matter
chartRules: Use direct labels and meaningful tick marks.
Provide data table or text summary equivalent.
Do not rely on green/red to distinguish series; add markers, dashes or labels.
Do not show percentages without a denominator or definition.
Do not use 3D charts, decorative pie charts or animated chart reveals.
Keep data density proportional to the decision being supported.

recommendedOperationalVisuals.name: stockThreshold
recommendedOperationalVisuals.visual: Horizontal quantity bar with a visible reorder marker and textual quantity
recommendedOperationalVisuals.textCompanion: On hand 420 kg · Reorder point 500 kg · Short by 80 kg

recommendedOperationalVisuals.name: productionFlow
recommendedOperationalVisuals.visual: Connected sequence: Raw materials → Work order → Finished goods → Dispatch
recommendedOperationalVisuals.textCompanion: Each stage shows state, timestamp, quantity and responsible person.
recommendedOperationalVisuals.use: Explain where a batch currently sits and what is blocking progress.

recommendedOperationalVisuals.name: movementHistory
recommendedOperationalVisuals.visual: Vertical ledger timeline with incoming/outgoing markers and linked references
recommendedOperationalVisuals.textCompanion: Date · Movement type · Reference · Quantity · Balance after movement

recommendedOperationalVisuals.name: paymentProgress
recommendedOperationalVisuals.visual: Paid / outstanding split bar with amount labels
recommendedOperationalVisuals.use: Understand a receivable or payable balance.

rules: Name the real-world object: item, purchase, batch, invoice, payment, stock adjustment.
Use action verbs that describe the result: Save draft, Post purchase, Record payment, Receive goods, Reverse entry.
Use units in every quantity context.
Use dates and currency consistently across all pages.
Do not use celebratory or vague messages for routine recordkeeping.
Do not expose database terms such as row, entity, payload or mutation to end users.

goodExamples.why: Shows a measurable gap and unit.

goodExamples.copy: Saved on this device · Waiting to sync
goodExamples.why: Does not falsely imply server persistence.

goodExamples.copy: Received quantity is 12 kg above the remaining purchase quantity.
goodExamples.why: Identifies the mismatch and its unit.

avoidExamples: 100% complete (when the system cannot substantiate the percentage)

productDefaultsBeyondMinimum: 44 by 44 CSS px target areas for primary touch controls
reduced-motion preference honored for all nonessential animation
all statuses communicated through text and icon/shape as well as color

successCriteria.name: Use of Color
successCriteria.implementation: Never encode error, success, selection, trend or status using color alone.

successCriteria.name: Contrast (Minimum)
successCriteria.implementation: At least 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text.

successCriteria.name: Resize Text
successCriteria.implementation: Support 200% text resize without loss of content or functionality.

successCriteria.name: Reflow
successCriteria.implementation: At 320 CSS px, preserve content and functionality without page-level two-dimensional scrolling; exempt only genuinely two-dimensional data where its use requires it.

successCriteria.name: Non-text Contrast
successCriteria.implementation: Meaningful component boundaries, controls and graphical objects need 3:1 contrast against adjacent colors.

successCriteria.name: Text Spacing
successCriteria.implementation: Allow user text-spacing overrides without loss of content or functionality.

successCriteria.name: Keyboard
successCriteria.implementation: All functionality is operable without a pointer.

successCriteria.name: Focus Order
successCriteria.implementation: DOM and visual order are coherent; focus follows the task sequence.

successCriteria.name: Headings and Labels
successCriteria.implementation: Labels describe the purpose of each field and action.

successCriteria.name: Focus Visible
successCriteria.implementation: Every keyboard-operated component has a visible focus state.

successCriteria.name: Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)
successCriteria.implementation: Sticky headers, drawers and floating layers must not fully hide the focused control.

successCriteria.name: Dragging Movements
successCriteria.implementation: Provide a click/tap alternative for reorder, drag and drop operations.

successCriteria.name: Target Size (Minimum)
successCriteria.implementation: Meet 24 by 24 CSS px minimum or an applicable exception; the product design target is 44 by 44 CSS px.

successCriteria.name: Error Identification
successCriteria.implementation: Identify the field and describe the error in text.

successCriteria.name: Error Suggestion
successCriteria.implementation: Provide a correction suggestion when it is known and safe.

successCriteria.name: Error Prevention (Legal, Financial, Data)
successCriteria.implementation: For financial and data-changing actions, provide reversibility, input checking with correction, or a review/confirmation mechanism.

additionalGoodPractice: Use semantic landmarks, headings, labels, table headers and live regions.
Use aria-live='polite' for routine asynchronous status; use assertive announcements only for urgent blocking errors.
Do not put essential instructions only in tooltips or hover states.
Keep error messages visible until corrected or clearly superseded.
Test with keyboard-only navigation, screen reader, browser zoom, high contrast and touch input.
Avoid auto-focusing a destructive action or moving focus after routine success.

motion.policy: Honor prefers-reduced-motion. Motion animation triggered by interaction can be disabled; this also aligns with WCAG 2.2 AAA 2.3.3.
motion.flashPolicy: Never create flashing attention effects; comply with WCAG 2.3.1.
motion.autoUpdatePolicy: For auto-updating regions, preserve user control and do not unexpectedly move focus.

accessibility.auditWarning: The color pairs in this file are programmatically checked token pairings only. Full WCAG conformance requires testing rendered components, text, hover/focus states, charts, keyboard flows, content reflow and assistive-technology behavior.

colorContrastAudit.method: WCAG relative luminance contrast ratio calculation
colorContrastAudit.scope: Selected semantic token combinations only, not a full UI conformance audit

inventoryPage.purposeLine: Raw materials, finished goods and stock movement history.
inventoryPage.note: All quantities above are visual examples only, not source requirements or actual MillLedger data.

processDiagram.title: Production trace
processDiagram.rule: Use a connected visual sequence with readable labels and stage details; do not replace the explanation with icons alone.

implementation.tokenConsumption: Components must consume semantic tokens. Avoid one-off hex values inside individual components.
implementation.cssNaming: Use stable CSS custom properties such as --ml-color-bg-canvas, --ml-color-text-primary, --ml-color-action-primary-bg, --ml-radius-control and --ml-motion-overlay-enter.
implementation.themeStrategy: Use semantic light/dark tokens behind a single theme attribute or class. Do not invert colors mechanically.

rules: Keep icon style consistent.
Do not use emoji as interface icons.
Icon-only controls require an accessible name and a sufficiently large hit area.
Pair status icons with words.

responsiveRules: Do not scale the desktop sidebar down into an unusable mobile rail.
Keep primary actions reachable without relying on hover.
Reflow page sections and forms at narrow widths.
Keep important identifiers visible when a table scrolls horizontally.
Avoid cumulative layout shift when loading, filtering or showing validation.
performanceRules: Prefer opacity and transform for transitions.
Do not animate width/height/position in ways that trigger repeated layout unless the interaction requires it.
Do not delay navigation or submission to finish an animation.
Reserve space for loading and validation feedback to prevent layout shift.
qualityGates: Run contrast checks for every text/background pair and every interactive boundary.
Check primary, secondary, disabled, hover, selected, error and focus component states.
Test browser zoom at 200% and text spacing overrides.
Test keyboard navigation and modal focus return.
Test offline, queued, syncing, conflict and retry states.
Verify success feedback appears only after authoritative commit.
Verify transaction review and correction/reversal behavior.
Review a real inventory table with large datasets and long labels; do not approve based only on a landing page.
